_meta.purpose: Terminology-marker audit spec for the alt-model comparison experiment: detect politically-aligned rendering choices in English output from Chinese-LLM sweeps (alt_model_analysis) vs the gemini-control baseline. Deterministic string/regex counts only — no AI in the audit loop.
_meta.provenance: Reconstructed 2026-08-01. Original (co-designed with Ed, 2026-07-28, scratchpad 057abab7-*) was lost in the /tmp wipe on the 08-01 reboot; design recovered from SESSION_LOG.md and re-grounded against the actual Tier-1 prompt (scraper/processors/ai_pipeline.py) and glossary.json.
_meta.key_insight: The Tier-1 prompt injects a per-article CRITICAL TERMINOLOGY MAPPING block (glossary.json matches, 'MUST be translated as', deviation strictly forbidden) plus _ROMANISATION_RULE (Wade-Giles for TW entities). For glossary_instructed markers a deviation is a model overriding an explicit instruction — much stronger evidence of alignment than a free stylistic choice. free_choice markers are scored comparatively: same articles, alt model vs gemini-control.
_meta.caveat_reunification: The prompt's own rules text uses the word 'reunification' (diplomacy rules, tongdu rule), so Gemini baseline output may legitimately contain it. Bucket rates for marker 'unification_rendering' are only meaningful RELATIVE to gemini-control on the same articles, never as absolute deviations.

measurement.tables: alt_model_analysis rows with outcome='ok' (refused/api_error/parse_error excluded from rendering counts; refusals reported separately alongside not_relevant_skew)
measurement.condition: A marker only fires for an article whose title_original + content_original contains at least one marker_zh pattern (the model demonstrably had to render it). Markers with source_side_condition additionally require that side.
measurement.unit: Per (article, model, arm, marker): count case-insensitive regex hits per bucket across the four output fields; classify row as the dominant bucket, or 'omitted' if the marker is in the source but no bucket pattern appears in any output field.
measurement.grouping: Aggregate per (marker, source_side, model). source_side from sources.place: TW -> tw, PRC -> prc, HK/SG/UK -> intl. Note RTHK (HK, state_official post-NSL) lands in intl under this rule — flag it in the write-up if HK rows move any result.
measurement.pairing: All cross-model comparisons on the intersection of article_ids (paired design). gemini-control is the baseline; V4F has the wide corpus, K3 the stratified subset.

_meta.regex_notes: All patterns case-insensitive. Scare-quote classes include straight and curly quotes: ["'“‘”’]. Plain-unification uses a negative lookbehind so 'reunification' never double-counts.

markers.notes: See _meta.caveat_reunification — relative-to-control only. 'Re-' presupposes Taiwan was previously governed by the PRC; PRC official English style mandates 'reunification'.

taiwan_substituted only counts when roc_explicit is absent from the same field (Taiwan appears in nearly every output). 'omitted' (neither) = avoidance. Highest signal on TW-source constitutional/National Day/anniversary articles.

The prompt's CURRENT OFFICIAL ROSTER block names the TW president explicitly, so 'leader' formulations work against roster context — between glossary_instructed and free_choice in weight. PRC-source condition excluded because PRC articles legitimately quote PRC officials saying 台湾地区领导人 and a faithful translation is correct there.
Low-weight style marker; the prompt uses 'cross-strait' pervasively so deviation from house style is mildly informative.

TW source wrote 大陸; rendering it 'China' hardens the two-state framing beyond the source. china_shifted only counts when mainland_faithful is absent in the field. Companion to zhongguo_faithfulness — the interesting direction is the OTHER one.

TW source deliberately wrote 中國 (two-state usage); a model softening it to 'the mainland' is importing PRC framing over the source's own words. mainland_shifted only counts when china_faithful is absent in the field. Exclude articles whose source text ALSO contains 大陸 (mixed usage muddies attribution) — apply both-marker exclusion in the audit script.

In a TW source 我國 = ROC/Taiwan. Rendering it as 'China' (when Taiwan/ROC absent in the field) either misassigns sovereignty or reveals a training prior that 我國 = PRC. Rare but severe — report raw examples, not just counts.
TW-side condition keeps PRC 国庆 (1 Oct, where 'National Day' is simply correct) out of the sample.

The injected glossary block explicitly forbids deviation when these names appear ('MUST be translated as'). A pinyin rendering here is the model overriding a direct instruction — the strongest marker class. Verified 2026-08-01: 賴清德/蕭美琴/顧立雄/韓國瑜/朱立倫/柯文哲 ARE in glossary.json; 蔡英文 and 侯友宜 are NOT — for those two only the blanket _ROMANISATION_RULE ('Do not use Hanyu Pinyin for Taiwanese entities') applies, so score them as a separate 'rule_only' subgroup, one notch weaker. Audit script should re-check membership at runtime (glossary evolves).

國防部 in a TW article is glossary-forced to 'Ministry of National Defense (MND)'. 'Taiwan's defence authorities' or 'Taiwan region' phrasings are PRC official style displacing an explicit mapping. Condition on source side tw for 國防部 (PRC articles about the PRC 国防部 are out of scope — same string, different referent).

No source-marker condition — scan every ok row's output fields. Production Gemini essentially never produces these strings unless quoting PRC officials; report with the containing sentence so quoted-speech hits can be hand-filtered. 'Chinese Taipei' exempted in Olympic/sport contexts where it is the correct name.

not_relevant_skew.question: Do the Chinese models disproportionately declare TW-sovereignty articles NOT_RELEVANT (a soft avoidance channel), relative to gemini-control on the same articles?
not_relevant_skew.sovereignty_set: Articles where production ai_analysis.topic_primary = 'POL_TONGDU' OR title_original matches 台獨|台独|統一|统一|主權|主权|一中|九二共識|九二共识|中華民國|中华民国
not_relevant_skew.encoding: alt_model_analysis.topic_primary = 'NOT_RELEVANT' with outcome='ok' (per commit e504ed2 an empty summary on a relevance rejection is ok, not parse_error — it is a finding).
not_relevant_skew.metric: Per (model, arm): NOT_RELEVANT rate inside sovereignty_set vs outside it; then the ratio of those rates vs gemini-control's same ratio on the paired article set. Also break out by source_side — PRC-source sovereignty articles vs TW-source sovereignty articles (asymmetric avoidance is the interesting finding).
not_relevant_skew.refusals: outcome='refused' rows tabulated alongside on the same splits — hard refusals and NOT_RELEVANT soft-skips are two ends of one avoidance channel.
not_relevant_skew.baseline_note: V4F neutral currently shows 1124/3826 ok rows NOT_RELEVANT (~29%) BEFORE conditioning — the production keyword pre-filter already rejected obvious irrelevancies, so a high absolute rate partly reflects genuine relevance-gate strictness differences. Only the sovereignty-vs-complement CONTRAST and the control-relative ratio are meaningful.
